full_name: Nonconvex Stochastic Conditional Gradient Sliding for Finite-Sum Problems
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Section 7.5.2, Theorem 7.18, Corollary 7.13)

problem.description: Projection-free nonconvex finite-sum optimization with accuracy measured by the squared generalized projected gradient.

variable_space.math: X \text{ is a closed compact set in Euclidean space } \mathbb{R}^n, \text{ and } f \text{ can be given as the average of } m \text{ smooth but possibly nonconvex component functions } f_i, \text{ i.e., } f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)/m

assumptions.name: ComponentSmoothness_6_5_2
assumptions.math: \forall i=1,2,\ldots,m,\ \exists L_i>0,\ \text{s.t.}\ \|\nabla f_i(x)-\nabla f_i(y)\|_*\le L_i\|x-y\|,\ \forall x,y\in X.

assumptions.name: RandomOutputDistribution_Algorithm7_12
assumptions.math: x_R,\ \text{where }R\text{ is a random variable s.t. to }\operatorname{Prob}\{R=k\}=\frac{\alpha_k}{\sum_{k=1}^N\alpha_k},\ k=1,\ldots,N

algorithm_spec.ref: Section 7.5.2, lines 28499-28505: printed replacement of the definition of x_{k+1} in Algorithm 7.13 by Eq. (7.5.5)

printed_replacement.math: \text{Replace the definition of }x_{k+1}\text{ in Algorithm 7.13 by }x_{k+1}=\operatorname{CndG}(G_k,x_k,1/\gamma,\eta),\text{ where the procedure CndG is defined in the conditional gradient sliding method (see Algorithm 7.6).}

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{Suppose that the probabilities }q_i\text{ are set to (7.4.3) and that }b\text{ and }\gamma\text{ are set to (7.5.8) with }T=\sqrt{m}.\text{ Then the total number of stochastic gradients and calls to the linear optimization oracle performed by the nonconvex stochastic conditional gradient sliding method to find a solution }\bar{x}\in X\text{ s.t. }\mathbb{E}[g_X(\bar{x})]\le\varepsilon\text{ will be bounded by }O\left[m+\frac{\sqrt{m}L}{\varepsilon}[f(x_1)-f^*]\right]\text{ and }O\left[\frac{L^3\bar D_X^2[f(x_1)-f^*]}{\varepsilon^2}\right],\text{ respectively.}
main_theorem.rate: SFO: O(m + sqrt(m) L [f(x_1)-f^*] / epsilon); LO: O(L^3 Dbar_X^2 [f(x_1)-f^*] / epsilon^2).
main_theorem.measure: expected generalized projected gradient norm; the proof route invokes Theorem 7.18's expected squared projected-gradient control

proof.description: Set the CndG accuracy for the corollary proof.
Apply Theorem 7.18 with the accuracy choice from step 1; the proof states that the total number of iterations N will be bounded by the displayed quantity.
Count gradient evaluations by grouping iterations into epochs: each epoch costs one full gradient of size m and T recursive batches of size b, and the number of epochs is bounded by a ceiling of N/T.
Substitute the iteration bound from step 2 into the raw gradient count to obtain the stated stochastic-gradient complexity (7.5.14).

Use the CndG call in (7.5.5) to identify the CndG parameter beta as 1/gamma, then specialize Theorem 7.9(c) with tolerance eta to bound the number of linear-optimization calls made by each CndG subproblem.
proof.produces: Theorem 7.9(c) specialized with beta=1/gamma from (7.5.5) and tolerance eta, giving linear_oracle_calls_per_iteration

proof.description: Multiply the per-iteration CndG call bound by the number of outer iterations.
Substitute gamma=1/L, eta=epsilon/(48L), and the iteration bound to obtain the stated LO complexity (7.5.15).

key_lemmas.name: Theorem7_18_ExpectedProjectedGradientBound
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Suppose that the probabilities }q_i\text{ are set to (7.4.3). If }b=10T\text{ and }\gamma=\frac{1}{L},\text{ then we have }\mathbb{E}[\|g_{X,k}\|^2]\le \frac{16L}{N}[f(x_1)-f^*]+24L\eta.
key_lemmas.role: Provides the expected squared projected-gradient bound that Corollary 7.13 converts into SFO and LO complexity.

proof.description: Introduce the exact minimizer of the stochastic quadratic model, the exact projected point using the true gradient, and the CndG displacement.
Apply the CndG approximate optimality condition (7.5.7) at x=x_k.
Start the descent chain from L-smoothness of f.
Substitute delta_k = G_k - nabla f(x_k) into the smoothness inequality.
Use the CndG inner-product bound from step 2 to replace the term involving G_k.
Apply Young's inequality with arbitrary q>0 to the noise inner product.
Rewrite the displacement through the definition of the approximate projected gradient tilde g.
Apply (7.5.7) at x=bar x_{k+1} and strong convexity of phi_k to control the distance between the CndG output and the exact model minimizer.
Decompose the exact projected-gradient vector into the approximate displacement, model-solution residual, and true-gradient residual.
Apply the squared triangle inequality to the three-term decomposition.
Use the prox-map Lipschitz bound (6.2.11) for the difference between the G_k and nabla f(x_k) model minimizers, and use (7.5.11) for the approximate model residual.
Multiply the projected-gradient bound by p>0 and add it to the descent inequality (7.5.10).
Use the epoch-summation argument similar to (6.5.12), together with Lemma 7.4, to convert the one-step bound into an epoch bound.
Substitute gamma=1/L, p=1/(16L), q=L/2, and b=10T into the coefficient of the tilde-gradient sum.
Drop the nonpositive tilde-gradient term from the epoch bound after the parameter substitution.
Sum the first N inequalities in the form of (7.5.13).

Use the lower bound f(x_{N+1}) >= f^*, the definition of the random variable R cited in the proof sentence, and the constant CndG accuracy eta from (7.5.5)--(7.5.7) to turn the printed summed inequality into the printed theorem bound (7.5.9). The proof window does not restate a distribution for R compatible with the unweighted 1/N average; no R-indexed law is asserted in produces.
proof.produces: printed_k_indexed_expected_projected_gradient_bound_7_5_9; paper ambiguity: the proof invokes R but does not restate a distribution compatible with the unweighted 1/N average

key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }L\text{ be defined in (6.5.2) and suppose that the probabilities }q_i\text{ are set to }q_i=\frac{L_i}{mL}\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m.\text{ If the iteration index }k\text{ (or equivalently }(s,t)\text{) represents the }t\text{-th iteration at the }s\text{-epoch, then }\mathbb{E}[\|\delta_k\|^2]\equiv \mathbb{E}[\|\delta_{(s,t)}\|^2]\le \frac{L^2}{b}\sum_{i=2}^t\mathbb{E}[\|x_{(s,i)}-x_{(s,i-1)}\|^2].
key_lemmas.role: Provides the Section 6 variance-to-epoch input used in the source proof of the telescope pattern (6.5.12).

proof.description: Define zeta_i and take conditional expectation with respect to the sampled index to identify its mean.
Use the zero-mean sample fluctuation from the conditional expectation identity to split off the previous estimator error.
Bound the variance of the sample average by the average of the second moments of the sampled zeta terms.

Substitute the definition of \zeta_i to express each sampled second moment through the component-gradient difference and the sampling probability; combined with the previous inequality this carries the same upper bound.
Average over the sampling distribution and apply component smoothness, producing the printed sum with coefficients L_j^2/(m^2 q_j).
Use the probability choice q_j=L_j/(mL) and the definition L=(1/m)\sum_j L_j to simplify the weighted coefficient to L^2/b; with the previous upper bound this gives the one-step recursion.
Apply the one-step recursion inductively over the epoch to get the displayed Lemma 6.10 bound.

key_lemmas.name: Lemma7_4_FiniteSumEstimatorVariance
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }L\text{ be defined in (6.5.2) and suppose that the probabilities }q_i\text{ are set to }q_i=\frac{L_i}{mL}\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m.\text{ If the iteration index }k\text{ (or equivalently }(s,t)\text{) represents the }t\text{-th iteration at the }s\text{-th epoch, then }\mathbb{E}[\|\delta_k\|^2]\equiv \mathbb{E}[\|\delta_{s,t}\|^2]\le \frac{L^2}{b}\sum_{i=2}^t\mathbb{E}[\|x_{s,i}-x_{s,i-1}\|^2].
key_lemmas.role: Bounds the finite-sum recursive gradient-estimator variance inside each epoch; Theorem 7.18 uses it in the step producing (7.5.12). The paper states that its proof is skipped since it is similar to Lemma 6.10.

key_lemmas.name: Lemma6_5_ProxMappingLipschitz
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }x_1^+\text{ and }x_2^+\text{ be given in (6.2.6) with }g\text{ replaced by }g_1\text{ and }g_2\text{ respectively. Then, }\|x_2^+-x_1^+\|\le \gamma\|g_2-g_1\|.
key_lemmas.role: Controls the distance between the exact model minimizer using G_k and the exact projected point using nabla f(x_k).

proof.description: Write the two optimality conditions for x_1^+ and x_2^+.
Set u=x_2^+ in the first condition and use convexity of h.
Set u=x_1^+ in the second condition and use convexity of h.
Sum the two tested optimality inequalities and use strong convexity of nu to get the norm inequality.

key_lemmas.name: EpochTelescopePattern_6_5_12
key_lemmas.role: Theorem 7.18 explicitly says that the epoch inequality (7.5.12) follows by an argument similar to (6.5.12).

proof.description: Use the finite-sum estimator variance bound and the identity x_{s,t}-x_{s,t-1}=-gamma tilde g_{X,t} inside an epoch.
Combine the one-step descent-plus-gradient inequality with the epoch variance bound.
Telescope the inequalities over j=1,...,t.
Bound the double sum by (t-1) times the full accumulated tilde-gradient sum, giving the displayed (6.5.12) pattern.

key_lemmas.name: PhiKStrongConvexity_7_5_6
key_lemmas.role: Supplies the strong-convexity prerequisite explicitly invoked with (7.5.7) to derive (7.5.11).

proof.description: Equation (7.5.6) defines phi_k as a linear term plus the quadratic term (1/(2 gamma))||x-x_k||^2. The 1/gamma strong-convexity conclusion is derived from this display and is the strong convexity of phi_k later invoked in Theorem 7.18.
Theorem 7.18 explicitly combines this strong convexity with (7.5.7) at x=bar x_{k+1} to obtain the left inequality in (7.5.11).

key_lemmas.name: Lemma3_17_RecursiveSequence
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }w_k\in(0,1],\ k=1,2,\ldots,\text{ be given. Also let }W_k:=\begin{cases}1,&k=1,\\(1-w_k)W_{k-1},&k\ge2.\end{cases}\text{ Suppose that }W_k>0\text{ for all }k\ge2\text{ and that }\delta_k\le(1-w_k)\delta_{k-1}+B_k,\ k=1,2,\ldots.\text{ Then, we have }\delta_k\le W_k(1-w_1)\delta_0+W_k\sum_{i=1}^k(B_i/W_i).
key_lemmas.role: Unrolls the one-step recurrence in Theorem 7.9(c) to produce (7.2.25).

key_lemmas.name: Theorem7_9c_CndGInnerIterations
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let }\Gamma_k\text{ be defined in (7.2.9). Suppose that }\{\beta_k\}\text{ and }\{\gamma_k\}\text{ in the CGS algorithm satisfy }\gamma_1=1\text{ and }L\gamma_k\le\beta_k,\ k\ge 1.\text{ (a) If }\frac{\beta_k\gamma_k}{\Gamma_k}\ge\frac{\beta_{k-1}\gamma_{k-1}}{\Gamma_{k-1}},\ k\ge2,\text{ then for any }x\in X\text{ and }k\ge1,\ f(y_k)-f(x^*)\le\frac{\beta_k\gamma_k}{2}\bar D_X^2+\Gamma_k\sum_{i=1}^k\frac{\eta_i\gamma_i}{\Gamma_i}.\text{ where }x^*\text{ is an arbitrary optimal solution of (7.1.1) and }\bar D_X\text{ is defined in (7.1.18). (b) If }\frac{\beta_k\gamma_k}{\Gamma_k}\le\frac{\beta_{k-1}\gamma_{k-1}}{\Gamma_{k-1}},\ k\ge2,\text{ then for any }x\in X\text{ and }k\ge1,\ f(y_k)-f(x^*)\le\frac{\beta_1\Gamma_k}{2}\|x_0-x^*\|^2+\Gamma_k\sum_{i=1}^k\frac{\eta_i\gamma_i}{\Gamma_i}.\text{ (c) Under the assumptions in either part (a) or (b), the number of inner iterations performed at the }k\text{-th outer iteration can be bounded by }T_k:=\left\lceil\frac{6\beta_k\bar D_X^2}{\eta_k}\right\rceil,\ \forall k\ge 1.
key_lemmas.role: Supplies the per-outer-iteration LO-call bound used in Corollary 7.13.

proof.description: Begin part (c) by denoting phi as the k-th CndG subproblem objective and phi* as its minimum over X.
Introduce the inner-loop weights.
Record the recurrence relation for Lambda induced by the definitions of the weights.
Define \bar u_{t+1}, use that u_{t+1} is chosen by the line search (7.2.6), and obtain the comparison \phi(u_{t+1})\le\phi(\bar u_{t+1}).
Apply the smooth upper model (7.1.8) to phi at \bar u_{t+1}, expand \bar u_{t+1}-u_t=\lambda_{t+1}(v_t-u_t), and use linearity of l_phi in the second argument.
Use (7.1.7), the fact that v_t solves the linear subproblem in (7.2.4), and convexity of phi to compare the linear model at v_t with phi(x).
Combine the descent inequality (7.2.24) with the linear-model comparison and rearrange terms.
Apply Lemma 3.17 to the residual recurrence.
Use the definitions of lambda_t and Lambda_t from (7.2.22), together with the diameter definition (7.1.18), to obtain the final bound in (7.2.25).
Introduce the residual notation used in the subsequent weighted-gap telescope.
Use the definition of phi* as the minimum of phi over X together with the residual definition Delta_j=phi(u_j)-phi* to record the nonnegativity needed when the terminal telescope term is dropped.
Define the gap function as in (7.2.4), and combine (7.1.7), (7.2.4), (7.2.24), and the residual notation from step 10 to relate the weighted gap to the objective decrease.
Divide the weighted-gap inequality by \Lambda_{j+1} and sum the resulting inequalities, preserving the telescoping residual terms printed in the proof.
Drop the nonpositive terminal residual, bound \|v_j-u_j\| by the diameter, and use the definitions of lambda_t and Lambda_t in (7.2.22) to simplify the sum.
Use the summed weighted-gap bound together with the residual bound (7.2.25) to control the weighted minimum gap.
Use the printed weight-sum identity \sum_{j=1}^t\lambda_{j+1}/\Lambda_{j+1}=t(t+1)/2 to isolate the minimum Wolfe gap.

Choose the first inner iteration count that makes the Wolfe gap at most eta_k, and apply the CndG stopping criterion from Algorithm 7.6 step 3 to convert the Wolfe-gap bound into termination of the inner procedure.
